title: Health and Performance
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Health and Performance in GCSE PE.
meta_desc: GCSE PE adventure on Health and Performance.
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Health and Performance.

concepts.def: A state of complete physical, mental and social wellbeing, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity, as defined by the World Health Organisation.
The ability to meet the demands of the environment and everyday tasks, often measured through components such as strength, stamina and flexibility.
The ability of the heart, lungs and blood vessels to deliver oxygen to working muscles during sustained exercise; also called aerobic endurance.
A way of living involving little or no physical activity, which raises the risk of obesity, heart disease and type 2 diabetes.
Eating the right amount of energy and the correct proportions of carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water for good health.
A condition of carrying excess body fat to the point that health is harmed, commonly identified by a body mass index (BMI) above 30.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Health and Performance — a core area of GCSE PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Health and Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Health and Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The World Health Organisation defines health as:
options: The absence of illness only
Complete physical, mental and social wellbeing
Having high fitness levels
Having a low body weight
Muscles and joints
Heart, lungs and blood vessels
Bones and ligaments
Nervous system

mcqs.q: A sedentary lifestyle increases the risk of:
options: Improved stamina
Obesity and heart disease
Stronger bones
Lower blood pressure

mcqs.q: Which BMI value is generally classed as obese?
options: Below 18.5
Over 30
Around 22
Just under 25

mcqs.q: Does being fit mean the same as being healthy?
options: No - you can be fit but unhealthy (e.g. injured or ill), and healthy without being very fit.
Eating only protein to stay healthy.
Health only means having strong muscles.
Fitness and health are exactly the same thing.

mcqs.q: What does a sedentary lifestyle lead to?
options: Improved cardiovascular fitness over time.
An increased risk of obesity, heart disease and type 2 diabetes.
No effect on health at all.
Health only means having strong muscles.

mcqs.q: What does a balanced diet require?
options: Eating only protein to stay healthy.
Cutting out fat completely.
Health only means having strong muscles.
The right amount of energy and the correct proportions of all nutrient groups.
